3D/4D Volume Geometry, Spatial Transforms, and NIfTI Export

Source: vignettes/volume-geometry.Rmd
volume-geometry.Rmd

Overview

Medical cross-sectional imaging (CT, MR, PET, SPECT) inherently captures 3D volumes across space and time. However, different software ecosystems adopt contrasting spatial coordinate systems:

  1. DICOM Patient Coordinate System (LPS):
    • +X+X: towards the patient’s Left
    • +Y+Y: towards the patient’s Posterior
    • +Z+Z: towards the patient’s Superior (head)
    • Defined by ImageOrientationPatient (FcolF_{col}, FrowF_{row} direction cosines) and ImagePositionPatient (S0S_0).
  2. Neuroimaging / NIfTI Coordinate System (RAS):
    • +X+X: towards the patient’s Right (inverted from LPS)
    • +Y+Y: towards the patient’s Anterior (inverted from LPS)
    • +Z+Z: towards the patient’s Superior
    • Represented by a 4×44 \times 4 homogeneous affine transformation matrix (sform) and quaternion rotation (qform).

dicomtk v0.2.0 introduces end-to-end, standards-compliant 3D/4D volume processing: - dicom_volume: An S3 class binding numerical voxel arrays with analytical affine matrices and slice metadata. - read_dicom_volume(): Geometry-aware reader for multi-slice directories and enhanced multi-frame DICOM IODs. - dicom_orientation(), dicom_to_lps(), dicom_to_ras(): Lossless spatial transformations. - dicom_pet_suv(), dicom_apply_voi_lut(), dicom_mr_rescale(): Modality-specific quantitative physics calibrations. - write_nifti(): dcm2niix-compatible NIfTI-1 export with BIDS JSON sidecars.

library(dicomtk)

1. Synthesizing Ground-Truth Medical Phantoms

For testing and reproducible research, dicom_synthesize() generates standards-compliant DICOM series for CT, MR, and PET modalities with known ground truth geometry, orientations (axial, coronal, sagittal, or oblique), and optional gantry tilt.

synth_dir <- tempfile("phantom_ct_")
dir.create(synth_dir, recursive = TRUE)

# Generate a 4-slice oblique CT phantom
phantom <- dicom_synthesize(
  out_dir = synth_dir,
  modality = "CT",
  dims = c(32L, 32L, 4L),
  spacing = c(0.8, 0.8, 2.5),
  origin = c(-20.0, -15.0, 10.0),
  orientation = "oblique",
  oblique_angles_deg = c(15, -10, 5),
  phi = FALSE
)

# Inspect synthesized files
length(phantom$files)
#> [1] 4

The returned generator object contains exact analytical ground-truth values for truth_affine_lps, truth_voxels, direction, and spacing.

2. Reading 3D Volumes with read_dicom_volume()

read_dicom_volume() inspects all slices in a folder, sorts them along the slice-normal trajectory, calculates the analytical 4×44 \times 4 voxel-to-world affine matrix, and verifies slice continuity:

vol <- read_dicom_volume(synth_dir)

# Print summary of S3 dicom_volume object
vol
#> <dicom_volume [CT] 32x32x4 | coord=LPS | units=HU>
#>   spacing: (0.8, 0.8, 2.5) mm | origin: (-20, -15, 10) mm
#>   frame_meta: 4 row(s) | provenance: 1 step(s)

# Inspect dimensions and affine matrix
dim(vol)
#> [1] 32 32  4
vol$affine
#>             [,1]      [,2]       [,3] [,4]
#> [1,] -0.21796232 0.7610010 -0.3613386  -20
#> [2,]  0.76666649 0.2039096 -0.3223960  -15
#> [3,]  0.06866532 0.1389185  2.4526507   10
#> [4,]  0.00000000 0.0000000  0.0000000    1

Checking Orientation

dicom_orientation() extracts the standard 3-letter patient anatomical direction code (e.g., LPS for axial, LIP for coronal, PIR for sagittal):

dicom_orientation(vol)
#> [1] "LPS"

sag_dir <- tempfile("phantom_sag_")
dicom_synthesize(out_dir = sag_dir, modality = "MR", dims = c(16L, 16L, 4L), orientation = "sagittal", phi = FALSE)
vol_sag <- read_dicom_volume(sag_dir)
dicom_orientation(vol_sag)
#> [1] "PIR"
unlink(sag_dir, recursive = TRUE)

3. Transforming Between LPS and RAS Coordinate Spaces

To interface cleanly between DICOM clinical viewers (LPS) and neuroimaging packages like FSL, SPM, ANTs, or FreeSurfer (RAS), use dicom_to_ras() (to_ras()) and dicom_to_lps() (to_lps()):

# Convert world coordinate frame from DICOM LPS to Neuroimaging RAS
vol_ras <- dicom_to_ras(vol)
vol_ras$coord_system
#> [1] "RAS"

# Anatomical axis directions remain invariant because voxel memory is unpermuted
dicom_orientation(vol_ras)
#> [1] "LPS"

# Inspect the negated X/Y rows of the 4x4 RAS affine
vol_ras$affine
#>             [,1]       [,2]      [,3] [,4]
#> [1,]  0.21796232 -0.7610010 0.3613386   20
#> [2,] -0.76666649 -0.2039096 0.3223960   15
#> [3,]  0.06866532  0.1389185 2.4526507   10
#> [4,]  0.00000000  0.0000000 0.0000000    1

to_ras() and to_lps() premultiply affine and direction by diag(c(-1, -1, 1, 1)) (a 180-degree rotation around the Superior ZZ axis, det⁡=+1\det = +1) without permuting in-memory voxel arrays, preserving right-handedness and physical world correspondence.

4. Modality Quantitative Transforms

Raw stored pixel values in DICOM are typically integers requiring physics calibrations before analysis.

PET Standardized Uptake Value (SUV)

PET scanners record radioactivity concentrations (BQML). dicom_pet_suv() calculates SUV normalized by patient Body Weight (bw), Lean Body Mass (lbm), or Body Surface Area (bsa), with radioactive half-life decay compensation:

pet_dir <- tempfile("phantom_pet_")
dicom_synthesize(out_dir = pet_dir, modality = "PT", dims = c(16L, 16L, 2L), phi = FALSE)
pet_vol <- read_dicom_volume(pet_dir)

# Compute body-weight SUV (g/ml)
pet_suv <- dicom_pet_suv(pet_vol, method = "bw")
pet_suv
#> <dicom_volume [PT] 16x16x2 | coord=LPS | units=g/ml>
#>   spacing: (1, 1, 2.5) mm | origin: (-16, -16, 0) mm
#>   frame_meta: 2 row(s) | provenance: 2 step(s)
unlink(pet_dir, recursive = TRUE)

Mammography & Radiography VOI LUT

For digital radiography (DX) and mammography (MG), dicom_apply_voi_lut() maps stored pixel values using standard DICOM PS3.3 LINEAR, LINEAR_EXACT, or SIGMOID transfer functions and automatically inverts MONOCHROME1 images:

mg_dir <- tempfile("phantom_mg_")
dicom_synthesize(out_dir = mg_dir, modality = "MG", dims = c(16L, 16L, 1L), phi = FALSE)
mg_vol <- read_dicom_volume(mg_dir)

mg_viewable <- dicom_apply_voi_lut(mg_vol)
range(mg_viewable$voxels)
#> [1] 0.3392436 0.8779687
unlink(mg_dir, recursive = TRUE)

Philips MR Private Scaling

Philips MR scanners store console display rescale parameters (0028,1052) / (0028,1053) alongside private quantitative scaling intercept (2005,100D) (ScaleIntercept) and slope (2005,100E) (ScaleSlope). dicom_mr_rescale() recovers floating-point physical values P=D/(RS⋅SS)P = D / (RS \cdot SS) per Chenevert et al. (2014):

mr_dir <- tempfile("phantom_mr_")
dicom_synthesize(
  out_dir = mr_dir,
  modality = "MR",
  dims = c(16L, 16L, 2L),
  extra_tags = list(
    RescaleIntercept = "0",
    RescaleSlope = "2.0",
    "(2005,100D)" = "0",
    "(2005,100E)" = "4.0"
  ),
  phi = FALSE
)
mr_vol <- read_dicom_volume(mr_dir)
mr_phys <- dicom_mr_rescale(mr_vol, philips_float = TRUE)
mr_phys
#> <dicom_volume [MR] 16x16x2 | coord=LPS>
#>   spacing: (1, 1, 2.5) mm | origin: (-16, -16, 0) mm
#>   frame_meta: 2 row(s) | provenance: 2 step(s)
unlink(mr_dir, recursive = TRUE)

5. Exporting to NIfTI-1 with BIDS Sidecar (write_nifti())

write_nifti() writes standards-compliant NIfTI-1 (.nii) files matching Chris Rorden’s dcm2niix specification:

  • Exact sform affine matrix in RAS coordinate space.
  • Exact qform quaternion rotation derived via polar SVD decomposition.
  • Companion BIDS JSON sidecar (<filename>.json) capturing scanner parameters (RepetitionTime, EchoTime, SliceThickness, SpacingBetweenSlices).
out_nii <- tempfile(fileext = ".nii")
bids_json <- sub("\\.nii$", ".json", out_nii)
write_nifti(vol, out_nii, json_sidecar = TRUE)

file.exists(out_nii)
#> [1] TRUE
file.exists(bids_json)
#> [1] TRUE

# Clean up
unlink(c(synth_dir, out_nii, bids_json), recursive = TRUE)

6. Full Backward Compatibility

All existing functions from dicomtk v0.1.0 remain fully functional: - read_dicom_series() delegates directly to read_dicom_volume(). - dicom_to_nifti() delegates directly to write_nifti().
